answer: Gating each identity's work rights on fresh proof-of-work blunts Sybil farming. A new identity must publish a header meeting an adaptive target before any quota is credited, so marginal cost is CPU time, not a one-time fee. Since the target rescales with total claimed identities, minting N costs about N times one grind while reward per identity stays capped. Building a harbor of ten thousand fakes each burns hours of hashing for one quota, so profit turns negative. Honest operators keep keys stored securely, so a gale of composite identities never hides a whisper of real work.
